gaps.moment: Any win at SMALL or above, centre figure; BIG and above also flies the tier name
gaps.current: The centre figure appears at its final value in one frame (hud.ts:362). Count-up exists only machine-side (juice.ts:358-372 pourCoins onCount, juice.ts:375 countUp) and in the Night receipt (nightCards.ui.ts:116-127). Burst and shake only at BIG+ (hud.ts:270-273).
gaps.proposal: Count-up: roll the centre figure from 0 to the amount over 0.5-1.1 s with ease-out (countUp pattern, juice.ts:375). Pitch each tick up with progress (procTickSemitones, charmProc.ts:22-25). Land with goldBurst (charmProc.ts:138) and the existing shake (hud.ts:272). Scale duration by tier.

gaps.where: src/machines/_base/juice.ts:150-187 celebrate(); design rule at juice.ts:2
gaps.moment: Win tiers big and above, before the reveal lands
gaps.current: celebrate() starts at impact: flash, pop, jingle, pour (juice.ts:161-176). The header at juice.ts:2 requires anticipation, action, impact, follow-through, but no windup stage exists. Anticipation exists only as nearMiss() for losses (juice.ts:315-331, 17 machine files), the Big One riser (bigone/index.ts:557) and the all-in arm (gambleFx.ts:33). tiers.ts:21 can classify the result before the reveal.
gaps.proposal: Anticipation: add windup(host, tier) run before celebrate for tier >= big. Play tensionRise (sfx.ts:883) with its param climbing 0 to 1 over 0.6 s (big/medium) or 1.2 s (huge+). Ramp lamp blink rate (l.blink, juice.ts:183) and add two slow zoom creeps (fx.zoomPunch, fx/types.ts:84). Fire celebrate on the last beat. Machines call await windup then void celebrate.

gaps.moment: Two matching reels with the third about to land (slot-style machines)
gaps.current: Near miss is a generic 0.7-0.9 s held breath (juice.ts:315-331: heartbeat, red pulse, vignette, zoom) before the losing face lands (pachislot/index.ts:404). The detector exists (reels.ts:155-158). No slowed last-reel deceleration was found by keyword in reels.ts.
gaps.proposal: Last-symbol tease: when nearMissLine flags two of three, decelerate the last reel over 0.8-1.2 s with ease-out and one reelTick per symbol passing (TRIM in sfx.ts:38-59). Land it with a soft cue after the loud pair, and keep the red pulse. Reuse the helper for other near-miss machines.

gaps.moment: A round where several charms proc in sequence
gaps.current: Each proc spawns an independent pop, a tick and a peg hop (hud.ts:398-401, charmProc.ts:28-30). Max 4 live pops (charmProc.ts:18). No running total links them.
gaps.proposal: Chain resolve: queue procs 120-140 ms apart in the order they resolve (left-to-right, as in Balatro). Each bounces its peg with the existing hop and pitch-ticks with procTickSemitones (charmProc.ts:22). End with a larger '= total' pop (popSize, charmProc.ts:124, size 2) and a goldBurst. Needs a per-round batch from the emitter (emitter not read).

notes:
Scope: read-only. Nothing was edited; no git writes, no servers, no Chrome. Research used WebSearch and WebFetch; URLs are inline below.

Verdict: machine-level juice is already deep (juice.ts tier table and celebrate escalation, the tiers.ts winFeel curve, nearMiss in 17 machine files, the pachislot tease). The biggest gaps are at the game layer and in anticipation. The centre win figure does not count up (hud.ts:362). juice.ts:2 requires an anticipation stage that celebrate() never runs. Quota, heat, overshoot and jackpot-pool moments are visually flat, and the heat meter exists in data but is never drawn.

Suggested order: gaps 1, 2, 5, 6, 8 first (all S effort, impact 4-5), then 3, 4, 7, 9. Gaps 10-15 are polish.

Design caution (Kelly counterpoint, https://gamedeveloper.com/design/video-indies-resist-the-urge-to-juice-it-or-lose-it- , GDC year conflicts across sources): heavy polish can cost immersion. For a casino ledger, keep the numbers readable and put the juice on the figure, not over it. New flashes should go through flashPrefs (juice.ts:44-50) and the reduceFlashing setting (fx.ts:12). HUD animations already switch off under prefers-reduced-motion (hud.css:187).

Research, with confidence:
- Balatro: scoring resolves piece by piece (chips, then mult), rolling digits, jokers trigger left to right with a bounce, shake scaled to score, rising pitch per scored card. Source is a third-party breakdown, https://blakecrosley.com/guides/design/balatro . Its numbers are illustrative and were not checked against the game. Developer intent (enjoying a scoring chain before knowing the outcome) is paraphrased from a video transcript, https://amara.org/videos/qZaMrU6iDy4J/en/4529388/15363640 . Medium confidence.
- Juice principles (tween, squash and stretch, shake, colour, easing, sound): secondhand summary of Jonasson and Purho's talk at https://rpgplayground.com/research-making-a-juicy-game/ . https://roblog.co.uk/2024/03/juicy-games/ names no specific techniques.
- Near miss, neuroscience: Clark et al. 2009, Neuron 61(3):481-490, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2658737/ . Near misses drove more activity than full misses in reward areas (ventral striatum, insula) and raised the wish to keep playing. The effect was tied to the player having control. Small sample of non-problem gamblers. High confidence in the finding, via search summary. Chase and Clark 2010 (J Neurosci) extended this to regular gamblers; secondary summary only.
- 2020 bioRxiv EEG preprint: faster re-initiation after a near miss. Preprint, not peer-reviewed as far as checked: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.10.08.330654v1
- Time-on-device and the 'machine zone': Schull, Addiction by Design, https://muse.jhu.edu/book/61897 (publisher summary). The reel-stop and near-miss audio claims come from low-quality blogs (https://www.tynmagazine.com/?p=229360 , gigwise) and are unverified. Treat them as hypotheses to playtest.
- Vampire Survivors: the developer drew on gambling-industry design, https://researchportal.port.ac.uk/en/publications/vampire-survivors-how-developers-used-gambling-psychology-to-crea/ . Gem pickups play a sound and fill a bar, https://www.thevibes.com/articles/lifestyles/53373/vampire-survivors-an-escalating-dopamine-rush-disguised-as-a-retro-game . Pitch escalation details were not found.
- Luck be a Landlord: not knowing the next symbol is itself rewarding, https://the-pixels.com/?p=144675 (secondhand review).
- CloverPit: reviews praise combo payoff and atmosphere, and criticise an item-pool lottery and repetition, https://trendingnow.games/reviews/cloverpit-review and https://www.pcgamesn.com/cloverpit/steam-roguelike-balatro . No juice-level analysis was found. Lesson: the payoff must be felt on every combo, not only the big one.
- Peglin: no usable results.

Not verified (flagged for follow-up): whether the quota-met stinger and cutscene fire on quota:met; whether jackpot pool readouts exist in world signage; the reel-stop driver (not read); the charm:proc emitter (not read); whether Hot stacks or Hungry already produce a toast elsewhere (only the files listed were read).
